name: Ahithophel
charge: Treason against David; counsel of incest; suicide
summary: David's counselor, whose word was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God, joined Absalom, advised him to take his father's concubines publicly, and asked for twelve thousand men to kill David that night. When Hushai's counsel was preferred, he went home, set his house in order, and hanged himself.
offense: Ahithophel's counsel was esteemed as though a man had inquired at the oracle of God. That reputation was shared in the days of David and Absalom (2 Samuel 16:23). Yet the weight men gave his advice did not make every purpose he served righteous. He left David and joined the conspiracy at Hebron (2 Samuel 15:12). His first recorded counsel in Jerusalem was for Absalom to go in to his father's concubines. It would make the breach with David unmistakable and strengthen those who had joined the rebellion (2 Samuel 16:20-22). The advice was politically calculated and morally corrupt. The prohibition concerning a father's wife did not change because violating it could secure a faction (Leviticus 18:8). He next proposed taking twelve thousand men to pursue David that night, strike the weary king, and bring the people back. He described peace for the multitude through the death of one man (2 Samuel 17:1-4). The promised settlement depended upon killing the king whom he had served. Skill in choosing a moment did not cleanse the betrayal at the centre of the plan.
judgment: David had prayed that Ahithophel's counsel would become foolishness. Hushai did not deny David's danger; he spoke of David's experience in war and urged a larger gathering with Absalom himself at its head. Absalom and the men of Israel preferred Hushai's answer (2 Samuel 17:5-14). The account gives the cause beyond the debate: the Lord had appointed the defeat of Ahithophel's good counsel to bring evil upon Absalom. “Good” described its effectiveness for the pursuit, not the righteousness of the enterprise. The counsel most likely to serve the rebellion was prevented from carrying it to its intended end.

entries.commentary: Absalom prepared chariots and horses and fifty men to run before him, rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate. When any man came to the king for judgment, Absalom called him, said his matters were good and right but there was no man deputed of the king to hear him, and wished that he himself were made judge in the land that he might do every man justice. This is the sneakiness Absalom did: he began to underhand the king, winning the love of the people behind the king's back, so that he could later betray him, as the prophecy said the sword would not depart from David's house.

When any man came near to do him obeisance, Absalom put forth his hand, took him, and kissed him, and on this manner he did to all Israel that came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel. Instead of going to the king and resolving things, Absalom got into the king's good graces, then went around patting people on the back and stroking them. This is what the bishop calls friendish, showing people friendship without being a true friend.

After forty years Absalom asked leave to go pay his vow in Hebron, and the king said, Go in peace. But Absalom sent spies through all the tribes to say, at the sound of the trumpet, Absalom reigneth in Hebron. Two hundred men went with him from Jerusalem in their simplicity, knowing nothing. Absalom also sent for Ahithophel, David's counsellor, and the conspiracy was strong, for the people increased continually with Absalom. This shows the simplicity of a lot of brothers in Israel: a man who says all the nice things and gains favor in your eyes goes completely against leadership and out of order, and you follow along carnally, not spiritually, because he kissed your hand and told you everything would be all right.

A messenger told David the hearts of the men of Israel were with Absalom, and David told his servants to arise and flee, lest Absalom overtake them suddenly and smite the city with the sword. The king went forth with all his household, leaving ten women who were concubines to keep the house, and all his servants and the Cherethites, Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites passed on before him. David, being the man of war that he is, saw everyone starting to follow Absalom, and instead of sitting there like a dummy, chose to leave and strategize while he was out.

The king told Ittai the Gittite to return, since he was a stranger and an exile who had only just come, and wished him mercy and truth. But Ittai swore that in whatever place the king was, in death or life, there also would his servant be, so David said, Go and pass over, and Ittai passed over with all his men and little ones. All the country wept as the people passed over the brook Kidron toward the wilderness. Ittai showed a level of loyalty that David respected, so David let him come. This loyalty in the face of trouble is the same thing seen throughout Israel's story.

Zadok and all the Levites bare the ark of the covenant, and David told Zadok to carry it back into the city, saying if he found favour in the eyes of the Most High, he would be brought again to see it and its habitation; but if not, let the Most High do as seemed good. He also told Zadok the seer to return with his son Ahimaaz and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, and to send him word. So they carried the ark again to Jerusalem. David sent the ark back in faith: make sure it stays in the city, and if it is the Most High's will, I will return. That is how much faith David had. Many of the songs in the book of Psalms were written while David was on the run like this, and some of it is prophecy of Christ, because the spirit of Christ was in every prophet.

David went up the ascent of Mount Olivet weeping, barefoot, his head covered, and all the people with him weeping. When told that Ahithophel was among the conspirators, David prayed that the Most High turn Ahithophel's counsel into foolishness. Then Hushai the Archite met him with his coat rent, and David sent him back to the city to feign service to Absalom and defeat Ahithophel's counsel, reporting all he heard to Zadok and Abiathar by their two sons. Ahithophel was such a good counsellor that his counsel was said to be like inquiring at the oracle of God, like talking to an angel of the Most High. So David prayed the Most High would turn that counsel into foolishness, and sent his friend Hushai to act like Absalom's servant so he could listen to Ahithophel's counsel and intervene. This was a game of chess, not checkers, and that is how we have to treat this thing today.

When David was past the top of the hill, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with saddled asses, two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine. When David asked where his master's son was, Ziba said Mephibosheth abode in Jerusalem, saying the house of Israel would restore him the kingdom of his father. So David gave Ziba all that pertained to Mephibosheth. Ziba came with gifts, and when David asked about Mephibosheth, Ziba claimed Mephibosheth thought the kingdom was about to be restored to him, which was not true. On that word David handed Ziba everything that belonged to Mephibosheth.

As David came to Bahurim, a man of the house of Saul named Shimei the son of Gera came out, cursing and casting stones at David and all his servants. Shimei cursed, calling David a bloody man and a man of Belial, saying the Most High had returned upon him all the blood of the house of Saul, and delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom his son, and taken him in his mischief because he was a bloody man. Shimei was of the house of Saul, and Saul was the wicked one who tried to kill David; it was by the hand of the Most High that Saul did not succeed. Yet Shimei cursed David as if David were in the wrong, because word gets around, people gossip and blame, and he saw David at a low state and went to rub it in his face. That is the mindset of some people in Israel as well.

Abishai the son of Zeruiah asked why this dead dog should curse the king, and offered to go take off his head. But the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, because the Most High hath said unto him, Curse David; who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so? David rolled with mighty men of war, so Abishai was ready to take Shimei's head off his shoulders. But David said to let him curse, for if it was of the Most High, then let him do it. Just as the Most High brings people to our forums and classrooms who bicker and try to bring confusion, it is of the Most High, sometimes to test the patience of those who pray for patience.

David said to Abishai and all his servants, Behold, my own son who came forth out of my bowels seeketh my life, how much more now may this Benjamite do it? Let him alone and let him curse, for the Most High hath bidden him. It may be that the Most High will look on his affliction and requite him good for the cursing this day. David reasoned that if his own son sought his life, this Benjamite was nothing; the Most High was doing this, so let him curse. It may be the Most High will look on all that was done to David and bless him in front of them, the same as when people try to bring us down and the Most High blesses us before them, which is why this congregation has grown exponentially.

David and his men went by the way while Shimei went along the hillside cursing, throwing stones, and casting dust; and they came weary and refreshed themselves. Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him. When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom saying, God save the king, Absalom asked why he went not with his friend, and Hushai answered that he would serve whom the Most High and Israel chose, and would serve in the presence of the son as he served the father. Hushai put into action the plan he and David made. Absalom challenged him, asking, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? Why wentest thou not with thy friend? This is a real friend, not a friendish one; a true friend tells you when you are wrong and full of it, not the one who only strokes your head and pats your back like Absalom did to steal the people's hearts.

Absalom asked Ahithophel for counsel, and Ahithophel said, Go in unto thy father's concubines whom he left to keep the house, and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father, and the hands of all with thee shall be strong. So they spread Absalom a tent on the top of the house, and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel. The counsel of Ahithophel was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God. Ahithophel counselled Absalom to lie with the ten concubines David left, in the sight of all Israel, on the roof of the house. This is the exact fulfillment of what the Most High spoke in chapter 12, that David's wives would be taken and one would lie with them in the sight of the sun, and that what David did secretly would be done before all Israel. It was not coincidence or irony; it was prophesied to happen, and none of it would have happened if David had not done what he did. The Most High keeps mercy and forgives, but by no means clears the guilty, so even when we come in and repent, we still must remember the fear of the Most High, for there is but one step between us and death.

Ahithophel had already given Absalom wicked counsel in the previous chapter, telling him to go in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel so that the hands of all that were with him would be made strong. Ahithophel was David's own counselor turned traitor, being the devil the Bible speaks of, working deceit and betrayal from inside the gates of Israel. His counsel in those days was regarded as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God. That tells you Ahithophel was very influential and had the gift of gab, so persuasive that his advice sounded almost biblical. Now he asks Absalom to let him choose out twelve thousand men to pursue David that same night while David was weary and weak handed, to smite the king only and bring back all the people. He wanted the victory and the bragging rights of being the one who killed King David.

Absalom wanted a second opinion, so he called Hushai the Archite to hear likewise what he would say. There is safety in a multitude of counselors, but only where the counsel is according to thus saith the Lord; a counselor who does not go to the scriptures is not one you should want. Hushai told Absalom that Ahithophel's counsel was not good at this time. He reminded him that his father and his mighty men were mighty and chafed in their minds as a bear robbed of her whelps, war ready and strategic, and that David would not lodge with the people but move by night. Hushai warned that if Absalom's men were overthrown at the first, even the most valiant warrior whose heart is as the heart of a lion would utterly melt, for all Israel knew David was a mighty man. This shows David and his mighty men were on another level; none of Absalom's thousands could compare to them. Instead Hushai counseled that all Israel be gathered from Dan to Beersheba as the sand by the sea, with Absalom going to battle in his own person. This deliberately inaccurate counsel would waste time gathering troops and give David room to escape; Hushai was a counterintelligence agent, a spy planted in righteousness, always siding with King David. Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

Hushai reported both Ahithophel's counsel and his own to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, telling them to send quickly and warn David not to lodge in the plains of the wilderness that night but to pass over speedily, lest he be swallowed up. The messengers Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited by En-rogel; a maidservant carried the word to them, but a lad saw them and told Absalom. The Most High put His spirit on certain people to orchestrate His plan; often when a man tries to do evil to another, it falls back on him, for he that diggeth a pit shall fall therein. They fled to a man's house in Bahurim that had a well, and a woman spread a covering over the well's mouth and ground corn upon it to camouflage it. When Absalom's servants came asking, she told them the men had gone over the brook of water, and the pursuers returned to Jerusalem. The two came up out of the well and told David to arise and pass quickly over the water. David and all the people passed over Jordan by the morning light, and there lacked not one of them that was not gone over.

When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he set his house in order and hanged himself. The evil counsel he devised reared its head around and bit its author; evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid. To be righteous is to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord; all unrighteousness is sin, and sin is the transgression of the law. David was righteous and did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while the sinner was pursued by his own evil.

David asks the Most High to give ear to his prayer and not hide from his supplication. You have to put yourself in the Bible and see yourself in these scriptures, the way Elder Kena, Bishop, and the leadership men teach. He mourns and makes a noise because of the voice of the enemy and the oppression of the wicked, who cast iniquity upon him and hate him in wrath. The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil. -

His heart is sore pained within him and the terrors of death are fallen upon him. Think about the condition we are in today; even keeping the commandments, we still suffer the same oppression, though the Most High covers those that keep them. When you drive, police will still jump behind you and run your plates, so make sure your tags are legal and not expired. The fearfulness and trembling and horror are written in the curses, the curses we did not learn in the Christian church. Many of the scriptures come back to these curses. -

He wishes for wings like a dove to fly away and be at rest, to wander far off and remain in the wilderness, hastening his escape from the windy storm and tempest. When these things come upon us many times you would think, if I could just get away, just leave this place. But the scriptures say we must serve out this punishment and endure much tribulation to enter the kingdom. Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield. -

He asks the Most High to destroy and divide their tongues, for he has seen violence and strife in the city. This is us being cursed in the city. You want to hasten your escape because you open the doors and go out into the world to work, shop, or school, and there is all this strife among our people. Moses dealt with the same thing when he left Pharaoh's house and found two men fighting. Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets. -

It was not an enemy that reproached him, which he could have borne, but a man his equal, his guide and his acquaintance, with whom he took sweet counsel and walked to the house of God. This is betrayal by someone you know well. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth. -

He asks that death seize the wicked and they go down quick into hell, for wickedness is in their dwellings, while he calls upon the Most High evening, morning, and at noon, and is heard and delivered. The Most High hears and afflicts them because they have no changes; there was no change in us, no repentance. Even when He pitied us and provided everything, bearing us on His wings, we rebelled and vexed His Holy Spirit, so He turned to be our enemy. -

The betrayer put forth his hands against those at peace with him and broke his covenant; his words were smoother than butter and softer than oil, yet were drawn swords, war in his heart. Cast thy burden upon the Most High and He shall sustain thee; He will never suffer the righteous to be moved, but bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days.

verses.text: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.
And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O Lord, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.
Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.

And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
And I will come upon him while he is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.
And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.

And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom.

And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.
Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.
For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:
But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance.
We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company.
